title: Put the Dots Back in an Address

concept.title: Four pieces of length 1 to 3, with a rule for each piece
body: An IPv4 address has four numbers from 0 to 255 separated by dots, and a number with more than one digit has no leading zero (`01` is not allowed, `0` is). You get the digits without dots and must put three dots back in every valid way. That is a search of depth **four**: for each of the four numbers choose its length (1, 2 or 3), check the piece, and continue.

The rule for a piece is checked **before** the piece is taken, so no invalid address is ever built. The depth is only 4 and each level has at most 3 choices, so there are at most 81 paths, whatever the input. The smaller length is tried first and the dot (code 46) is smaller than a digit (code 48), so the addresses come out in dictionary order.

statement: Given a string of digits, insert three dots to make a valid IPv4 address: four numbers from 0 to 255, each written without a leading zero (the number 0 is written as `0`), using all the digits in order. Print every valid address in dictionary order, one per line. If there is none, print `-1`.
inputFormat: The only line has the digits.
outputFormat: The addresses in dictionary order, one per line, or `-1`.
hints: The address has exactly four parts, and each part has 1, 2 or 3 digits.
A part must be at most 255 and must not start with 0 unless it is just 0.
The four parts must use all the digits: check that at the end.

explanation: Four levels, each choosing a part of 1 to 3 digits. A part with a leading zero or a value above 255 is skipped. After four parts, the address is recorded only if all digits were used.
solution.complexity: Time O(1): at most 81 paths of depth 4.
